title: Fix zsh 'no such file or directory' by finding the correct path on macOS
summary: zsh says 'no such file or directory' when the path you typed does not match a real file or folder. The usual causes are a typo, a different current folder, or a space in the name. Check where you are, find the real name, and run the command again with the correct path.

aliases.text: zsh no such file or directory
no such file or directory mac terminal
file not found in terminal mac
терминал no such file or directory
zsh net takogo fayla ili papki

error_patterns: zsh:1: no such file or directory

steps.explain: Check which folder Terminal is in right now. zsh resolves a relative path (one that does not start with / or ~) from this folder, so the same name can work in one folder and fail in another.
steps.expect: A full path such as /Users/yourname/Documents. This is the folder that relative paths start from.

steps.explain: List the files and folders in the current folder, including hidden ones. Compare the name with your command letter by letter: capital letters and the extension count, so Report.pdf is not report.pdf or Report.PDF.
steps.expect: A list of names with permissions and dates. If your file is listed, use its exact name; if it is not, go to the next step.

steps.explain: Search your home folder for the file by its exact name. Every match is printed with its full path; copy the right one. Use the name without any folder part.

placeholders.name: FILE_NAME
placeholders.description: Exact name of the file or folder, without its path.

steps.expect: One or more full paths, such as /Users/yourname/Documents/Report.pdf. No output means no item with that exact name exists in your home folder.

alternatives.explain: Search the whole Mac with Spotlight, which is faster on large disks. It finds files by the names in its index, so a very new file may take a moment to appear.

placeholders.name: FILE_NAME
placeholders.description: Exact name of the file or folder, without its path.

alternatives.expect: Full paths of the matching files, one per line.

steps.explain: Go to the folder that holds the file, so you can use its short name. Use the folder part of the path from the search, which is everything before the file name.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Folder that contains the file, taken from the search output.

steps.gui: In Terminal, type cd and a space, drag the folder from Finder into the Terminal window, then press Return.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt is now in that folder, and pwd shows its path.

alternatives.explain: Do not change folders. Give the full path to the file in your original command instead, which works from any folder.

placeholders.name: FULL_PATH
placeholders.description: Full path to the file, taken from the search output.

alternatives.expect: The file's details are printed, with no 'no such file or directory' message.

steps.explain: Run your original command again, now with the correct file name or the full path. Keep every capital letter and symbol exactly as the search showed them.

verify.expect: Your file is in the list, and the command no longer prints 'no such file or directory'.

warnings: A folder name with spaces must be quoted or escaped, for example cd 'My Folder', because zsh ends the path at each space.
Do not type a name from memory. Copy it from ls or the search output, because a wrong capital letter or extension gives the same error.

source.title: zsh manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
